items.title: 68087_Cliff Leeman oral history interview
items.q: To get back to the Condon band, when I went in with Eddie in '51... And we played with that band

ctx.x: ... your dear friend Walter Page, which was part of that great rhythm section known as one of the world's greatest.

I'm not particularly in love with guitars and banjos or anything that get in the way, I love a rhythm section with bass, piano and drums. There's enough configuration going on there. But Eddie Condon is an unsung hero; people never gave him credit for it -- he had a wonderful sense of chord progressions and so forth. He played the guitar, because it was unamplified, and never did get in the way. And it was just a joy to work with him, and all I could do was feel him a little bit here and there; he knew what to…

But they had a format, that front line, Wild Bill Davison, all through the years with me playing down there with him, a great cornet player, who is well reknowned now, but I got to know him backwards, that's why they bring me over to Switzerland every year to play
